text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
QADISSIYA
- National Assembly ratifies oil deal with Russia
- A Turkish delegation is in Iraq to discuss ways of implementing a gas deal with Iraq.
- Some 173,000 tonnes of foodstuffs under oil-for-food deal with United Nations arrive in Iraq.
- More ships loaded with foodstuffs expected to arrive at southern ports in coming days.
- Trade ministry to supply bakeries with subsidised flour.
- Iraq signs 500 health contracts with foreign firms.
- Food and medical supplies arriving in Iraq are scrutinised before reaching local markets.
- Kurdish rebels steal rations under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with U.N.
- Iran freezes trade relations with New Zealand.
- Tension escalates between Iran and the European Union.
- Palestinian woman opens fire on a crowd of Israelis.
(The above were also carried by THAWRA and JUMHOURIYA)
- Interior ministry holds symposium on smuggling.
THAWRA
- Editorial on the biased interpretations of U.N. resolutions on Iraq by the United States.
- Commentary on how badly the United States treats its European partners.
- Commentary on the failure of the United States to bring about peace in the Middle East.
- Article on role of financial incentives in boosting production.
JUMHOURIYA
- Seven new platforms added to the southern port of Umm Qasr to accomodate flurry in external trade.
